findings: All 18 frozen member hashes matched. The bounded prepare_fit_packet.py --review-targets-only replay reproduced the same complete map and reported no packet created.

The digest handoff is restricted to exact resolved allowlisted regular files. Hashing compares path and open-descriptor identity before and after the full streaming read, checks bytes read against the initial size, and issues an unapproved receipt until observed bytes equal both the campaign expected SHA-256 and mounted portable-registry SHA-256. Authorization re-stats the path and rejects changed identity.

Reuse is limited to an authorized exact path and the unchanged full stat tuple; it also requires agreement with the pinned verifier's device/inode/size/mtime/ctime arguments. A miss or stale identity calls the pinned original _content_digest. Only that digest callback is wrapped; the pinned portability metadata and registry digest comparisons remain, as do split source checks and membership validation. The integration test exercises changed same-size bytes with restored mtime and observes fallback plus rejection.

Input identity ordering remains fail-closed: expected and registry hashes are persisted before raw hashing; observed digest/size and footer results are persisted before authorization; the two hashes and expected size must match; the original portable registry is bound only after its hash and all source identities pass. The wrapper is installed before the initial load_campaign_split, and the worker imports and invokes the pinned trainer in-process, so the exact-stat handoff remains worker-local across the serial seeds.

Runtime counters are written atomically immediately after initial split validation, after each seed, and on abort where staging completed. Per-file hit/miss/fallback counts and avoided bytes from the first split load are separated from later calls that the original lru_cache already served; the frozen plan makes no speedup or fit-time forecast.

Compared with the reviewed fit-v2 candidate, recipe, evaluation, input-identity contract, resource policy, fit budget, grader/evaluator and pinned source archive are byte-identical. The added execution optimization changes no training target, model, split, seed, checkpoint selection, prediction or scoring semantics.

limitations: This is a static integration review plus focused synthetic tests. It does not demonstrate a Kaggle throughput improvement or authorize fit/provider work; packet, quota, profile, and root admission gates remain separate.

Stat binding detects changes at authorization and lookup but does not lock a mounted raw file against concurrent mutation after a successful lookup; the design relies on the admitted read-only mounted input source.
